title: Upper-storey "Enter Walkthrough Here" spawns the camera below / intersecting the floor slab
status: IMPLEMENTED / AUTOMATED GREEN / MANUAL RETEST REQUIRED
reproduction_path: 2C17 PROSTH. LAB -> Radiopharmacy (Second Floor) -> Enter Walkthrough Here
observed_defect: The targeted walkthrough spawn dropped the camera at (or below) the whole-model band datum (~ground/first floor) instead of the selected upper-storey room floor + eye height, so the camera started below / passing through the second-floor slab.

root_cause.pipeline_correct_end_to_end: resolveClinicalRoomWalkthroughSpawn uses the room's authoritative floor (fp.volume?.zLow ?? fp.floorZ) + WALKTHROUGH_EYE_HEIGHT_M and rejects wrong-storey rooms via programStoreyRanges; resolveTargetedWalkthroughSpawn returns spawn.z = roomFloorZ + eyeHeight; enterWalkthrough sets the initial camera position (start) to the override correctly.
root_cause.primary: In walkthroughController.enterWalkthrough the per-session floorElevation (the Z the camera is pinned to) was derived from the whole-model STOREY-BAND datum (chosen.zLow from loadStoreys Z-banding), not from the supplied targeted spawn. applyCamera re-derives the eye Z every frame via eyeZForFloor(floorElevation, WALKTHROUGH_EYE_HEIGHT_M), so the correct upper-storey spawn.z was overwritten on the first frame by the low band datum, dropping the camera below/through the slab.
root_cause.why_only_upper_storeys: For a ground/first-floor room the band datum ~= the room floor, so the eye Z was approximately correct and the defect was invisible. On an upper storey the band datum is far below the room floor, so the clobbered eye Z landed below the slab.

fix.change: Renamed the storey-band datum to storeyFloorZ and derived the per-session floorElevation from a new pure helper resolveWalkthroughFloorElevation(): when a finite targeted spawn override is supplied, floorElevation = spawnOverride.z - WALKTHROUGH_EYE_HEIGHT_M (reconstructs the selected room's own floor using the SAME canonical eye height the resolver applied); otherwise falls back to storeyFloorZ (generic entry unchanged).
fix.seam_extracted: frontend/src/components/spatial/walkNav.ts::resolveWalkthroughFloorElevation (pure, @itwin-free, unit-testable). The controller imports and calls it so runtime and tests share one implementation.
fix.post_spawn_floor_constraint: Because floorElevation now equals the room floor, applyCamera's eyeZForFloor(floorElevation, eye) reproduces spawn.z EXACTLY on entry and stays pinned there through forward/strafe/turn (no vertical drift, no snap to first floor, no slab pass-through). The floor constraint remains ACTIVE.

authorities_reused.room_floor_authority: fp.volume?.zLow ?? fp.floorZ (authoritative room footprint floor), reconstructed exactly via spawnOverride.z - eye
authorities_reused.eye_height_authority: cameraNav.WALKTHROUGH_EYE_HEIGHT_M (single shared constant used by resolver AND camera; no second eye-height authority introduced)

fix.graceful_fail: When no targeted spawn is supplied or the override is non-finite, the helper returns the storey-band datum (prior generic-entry behavior). The targeted resolver itself still returns NO_SAFE_WALKTHROUGH_SPAWN honestly when no defensible interior floor point exists.
fix.no_free_flight: No vertical-fly controls added; pitch continues to rotate the view only. The walkthrough remains a floor-constrained pedestrian.
fix.resolver_unchanged: targetedWalkthroughSpawn.ts and its 16 sub-property behavior are unchanged (it was already correct).

spawn_calc_before_after.before: start = spawnOverride (correct); floorElevation = chosen.zLow (whole-model band datum); eyeZ_per_frame = eyeZForFloor(band_datum, eye)  => below the upper-storey slab
spawn_calc_before_after.after: start = spawnOverride (correct); floorElevation = spawnOverride.z - eye (room floor); eyeZ_per_frame = eyeZForFloor(roomFloor, eye) == spawnOverride.z  => pedestrian eye height inside the room

cases: (a) upper-storey targeted spawn.z ~= roomFloorZ + eyeHeight AND the old storey-band pin is proven to land below the second-floor slab
(b) same-XY rooms on different storeys yield DISTINCT camera Z separated by the storey gap (fails if both collapse to one global Z)
(c) irregular/concave (L-shaped) upper-storey room: resolved interior XY is inside the footprint and Z sits on the correct storey
(d) post-spawn floor constraint is invariant across simulated XY movement: eye Z stays == spawn.z, above the slab, zero vertical drift
(e) spawn point in-room AND a representative equipment envelope in-room (containment sanity; spawn is room-derived, equipment is not the authority)
seam: override path uses spawnOverride.z - eye
seam: no-override falls back to storey-band datum
seam: non-finite override / non-finite eye falls back to storey-band datum
seam: eyeZForFloor(resolveFloor(spawnZ), eye) round-trips to spawnZ exactly

regression_preserved.scanner_acceptance: PASS (no changes to acceptance / equipment gate / canonical identity)
regression_preserved.all_prior_walkthrough_tests: PASS (walkNav, firstPerson, cameraNav, build1a walkthrough suites green)

limitations: The room floor is reconstructed as spawnOverride.z - eye; this is exact because the resolver and the camera share the single WALKTHROUGH_EYE_HEIGHT_M constant. If a future change gave the resolver a different eye height, the shared-constant invariant (covered by the round-trip test) would need to hold.
Generic (non-targeted) walkthrough entry still uses the storey-band datum, which is correct for whole-model entry and out of scope for B1B-MA-02.
Storey membership for the targeted spawn is still decided upstream by programStoreyRanges; this fix only ensures the controller honors the room floor the resolver already validated.
manual_retest_steps: Load MRTway Medical Clinic Demo; confirm /viewer renders at http://localhost:3000/viewer.
Select the 2C17 PROSTH. LAB clinical function and its Radiopharmacy room on the Second Floor.
Confirm the camera starts at standing eye height INSIDE the room, on top of the second-floor slab (not below/through it).
Walk forward/back/strafe and turn: the eye height must stay constant on the second-floor plane with no drop to the first floor and no slab pass-through.
Regression: repeat B1B-MA-01 (2D18 TECH. OFFICE -> PET/CT Scanner Room -> Discovery MI) and a ground-floor Enter Walkthrough Here to confirm both still behave correctly.
